heading: FortiGate observation worksheet
introduction: Run one check at a time in the authorized FortiGate console and correct VDOM/VRF. Replace <BGP_PEER_IP> with the actual peer IPv4 address; never paste the angle-bracket label literally. These examples are not tested customer output.
privacyNote: Keep outputs private and sanitize addresses, names and topology before sharing. No tunnel reset, BGP clear, configuration edit or continuous debug is included. The capture is bounded by packet count, not elapsed time.

checks.observation: Match the named check and member to the incident worksheet. Record alive/dead state, measured quality and SLA status without assuming they validate application service.
checks.limit: A healthy probe proves only its configured measurement. It does not establish BGP reachability, the selected application rule or the return path.
checks.stop: This is a snapshot. Stop if the command differs on this build or your role cannot inspect the required context; consult the installed-version documentation.

checks.observation: Find the intended peer and record its state and prefix information. Compare this result with the same timestamp's route and probe evidence.
checks.limit: An established neighbor is not proof that the required application prefix is present or that the application can communicate in both directions.
checks.stop: Save the relevant excerpt privately and return to the prompt. Do not clear or restart a neighbor to make the output look different.

checks.purpose: FortiGate: inspect the route toward the peer
checks.observation: Compare the selected route and interface with the intended healthy overlay and peer source. Repeat in the same routing context as the incident.
checks.limit: This routing view is not a packet capture. It must be compared with installed kernel state and observed egress when the views appear inconsistent.
checks.stop: Replace the peer label before running. If there is no matching route, record that result and investigate; do not insert an unreviewed static route.

checks.observation: Identify entries for the actual probe destination and BGP peer. Relate their interfaces and source constraints to the destination-role worksheet.
checks.limit: The existence of a probe-related route after failure can be expected. It does not alone prove that this route caused the application's outage.
checks.stop: Output can be large; use only when needed and save only relevant excerpts privately. Do not delete kernel entries or alter route priorities during collection.

checks.command: diagnose sniffer packet any 'host <BGP_PEER_IP> and tcp port 179' 4 30 l
checks.purpose: FortiGate: observe a bounded BGP traffic sample
checks.observation: After replacing the peer label, inspect interface names, direction and peer addresses. Verbosity 4 includes interface information; 30 limits matching packets.
checks.limit: Thirty packets is not a time limit. No matching packets may leave the command waiting; absence of captured traffic is not by itself proof of an outage.
checks.stop: Press Ctrl+C after at most 15 seconds or sooner if sufficient evidence is collected; otherwise it ends after 30 matching packets. Do not change offload settings or leave it unattended.
